title: Can we tell the sign of an answer in advance?
description: Six cases of adding or taking away positive and negative numbers are sorted by the signs of the numbers involved. Every subtraction is turned into adding the additive inverse, and the cases with the same signs have a fixed sign while the cases with different signs depend on the numbers. The video breaks the slip of thinking that taking away always makes a number smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn each subtraction into an addition, then ask whether the two numbers have the same sign or different signs. Watch for students who think that taking away a negative number must give a negative answer.

video_script.why: The child decides the sign of six kinds of sums and differences by turning each subtraction into an addition and comparing the signs.
video_script.substitution: The book's six cases, each tested on the number line and with the rule that subtraction is the addition of the additive inverse.
video_script.anchor: the six cases of the book written in two rows of three cards
video_script.payoff_line: Three cases have a fixed sign, and three can be either

final_answer.value: a. positive; b. can be positive or negative; c. negative; d. can be positive or negative; e. negative; f. can be positive or negative
final_answer.spoken: positive; positive or negative; negative; positive or negative; negative; positive or negative

hold_back: a. positive; b. can be positive or negative; c. negative; d. can be positive or negative; e. negative; f. can be positive or negative
never_show: the sign of any case before its step
maths_rules: (positive) + (negative): subtract the smaller from the greater and keep the sign of the greater; 5 + (−2) = 3 and 2 + (−5) = −3
when the two numbers are additive inverses the answer is zero, e.g. 3 + (−3) = 0
video_script.design: The six cases sit as cards. Each subtraction card flips into an addition card, then the cards sort into a fixed-sign group and a depends-on-the-numbers group, tested with number pairs.

<bookmark mark='known'/>A sum of two positive numbers is always positive. But positive take away positive can be either.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six more cases follow, and we must say what each one gives.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we tell the sign of the answer before we know the numbers?

<bookmark mark='inv'/>The number that gives zero when added is called the additive inverse.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Taking away a number is the same as adding its additive inverse.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to say if each answer is positive, negative or can be either.

beats.on_screen: subtraction becomes addition of the additive inverse: positive − negative = positive + positive; negative − positive = negative + negative; negative − negative = negative + positive

<bookmark mark='a'/>Positive take away negative becomes positive plus positive.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Negative take away positive becomes negative plus negative.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Negative take away negative becomes negative plus positive.

beats.on_screen: same signs: positive + positive is positive (case a); negative + negative is negative (cases c and e)

beats.moves_through: two arrows join end to end on the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step two, when both signs are the same, the answer's sign is clear.
<bookmark mark='pos'/>Two positives always give a positive, and positive take away negative is one of them.
<bookmark mark='neg'/>Two negatives always give a negative.
That covers negative plus negative, and negative take away positive.

beats.on_screen: different signs (case b): take the smaller number from the greater and keep the sign of the greater; 5 + (−2) = 3; 2 + (−5) = −3

beats.removed: the cards with the same signs

narration: <bookmark mark='diff'/>Step three, positive plus negative has different signs, so the answer depends on the numbers.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Take the smaller number from the greater, and keep the sign of the greater.
<bookmark mark='ex1'/>Five plus minus two gives three, which is positive.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Two plus minus five gives minus three, which is negative.

beats.on_screen: negative + positive (case f): (−5) + 2 = −3 and (−2) + 5 = 3; negative − negative (case d): (−5) − (−2) = −3 and (−2) − (−5) = 3; if the two numbers are additive inverses the answer is 0

marks.sw: the card negative + positive is picked out
marks.dd: the card negative − negative flips into negative + positive

beats.moves_through: the pointer jumps along the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='sw'/>Step four, negative plus positive is the same, whichever number comes first.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Minus five plus two gives minus three, and minus two plus five gives three.
<bookmark mark='dd'/>Negative take away negative becomes negative plus positive, so it can be either too.
<bookmark mark='exd'/>Minus five take away minus two gives minus three. Minus two take away minus five gives three.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>If the two numbers are inverses, the answer is zero.

beats.on_screen: check the sure cases with numbers: 5 − (−2) = 5 + 2 = 7; (−5) + (−2) = −7; (−5) − 2 = −7

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check each sure case with numbers.
<bookmark mark='c1'/>Five take away minus two is five plus two, which is seven.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Minus five plus minus two is minus seven. Minus five take away two is also minus seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three cases have a fixed sign, and three can be either.
<bookmark mark='fixed'/>Positive take away negative is positive. Negative plus negative is negative, and negative take away positive is too.
<bookmark mark='vary'/>Positive plus negative, negative take away negative and negative plus positive can be positive or negative.
